text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek lobbied for the country's membership of NATO and of the United Nations Security Council while attending a UN general assembly in New York.
- Slovenia's only choice for the future is integration into European communities, President Milan Kucan said at the celebration of the sixth anniversary of the country's independence on Wednesday.
- Erhard Busek, a coordinator of the South-European Cooperation Initiative (SECI) said Slovenian Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler confirmed that Slovenia will participate in activities of the group.
- Parliament started procedures to change the constitution in order to enable foreigners to buy land in line with European Union demands.

- U.S. Senator Robert Dole, who visited Slovenia this week, said Slovenia should continue lobbying for full membership in NATO despite lack of support from the White House as the final decision on new members has not been reached yet.
- Soldiers of the U.S. aircraft carrier John F. Kennedy, which is due to leave Slovenia's port Koper on Thursday, will participate in a Slovenian army exercise on the same day.
- A railway link between Slovenia and Hungary will be constructed by the year 2000, Slovenia's Minister of Traffic Anton Bergauer said at an international traffic conference in Helsinki.
- Statistics show one out of every three Slovenians has a car, while about 28 percent of all cars in the country were made by Serbia's Zastava, the largest car producer in the former Yugoslavia.
- Parliament is expected to vote on an extra tax on new cars on Thursday.
